todo_line: - [ ] 008 Implement the approved browser step plumbing and enable the iteration-066 journey, preserving its no-composer, privacy, no-auto-add, welcome, and no-Admin-conversation-access assertions.
outcome: The approved iteration-066 browser journey runs in Chromium without `@todo`, following Eve's real Request access interaction through Dan's email-linked read-only preview and explicit Add, then Eve's welcome return, while retaining every stated privacy and no-automatic-admission assertion.
scope: Implement browser definitions and support for the 16 currently undefined steps in `custom_group_access_request.feature`; reuse the two existing definitions for hidden Board conversations/member list and avoid duplicate or ambiguous step registrations.

Build the KMC/Alice/Dan/Eve/Board scenario state with the existing acceptance setup APIs: Alice and Dan are club admins, Eve is an ordinary active member, and Alice is Board's only member. Keep the scenario's identities and business wording unchanged.

Drive Eve through the actual Board placeholder in her reusable member browser context. Assert the Request access control is present, no message composer or group tabs/list content is exposed, click the real request control once, and observe the accepted-for-send status in the connected LiveView.

Capture request-email state before submission, allow the existing delivery pipeline to complete using established acceptance helpers, locate Dan's ordinary Admin recipient email for `Access request: Board`, and follow the HTML action identified by `Add Eve to Board` to the emitted club-hosted `/groups/:group_id/members/add/:person_id` URL. Do not synthesize the target URL from fixture IDs as a substitute for exercising the email link.

On Dan's targeted Members page, assert the resolved Eve/Board Add action is visible and that merely sending the request or opening its link has not admitted Eve. Click the accepted `#targeted-group-member-add` control and observe the success/member-row transition before asserting authoritative membership.

Capture the welcome-email baseline before explicit Add, identify Eve's normal Board welcome email, and follow its emitted Board link in Eve's browser context. Assert Eve can now see Board's conversation surface while the Admin access-request conversation remains unavailable and absent.
Remove only the feature-level `@todo` marker after the journey is fully defined and passing; retain `@journey` and `@iteration-066` provenance and preserve all scenario steps verbatim.

Add focused JavaScript tests only where useful for nontrivial new mailbox/link parsing or support behavior, and keep helper ownership coherent with the existing custom-group, mailbox, and per-member harness modules.
scope_exclusions: Do not change the journey's wording, remove or weaken any no-composer, hidden-conversation, hidden-member-list, no-auto-add, welcome, or Admin-conversation privacy assertion, or split the approved single journey into different scenarios.
Do not edit the focused domain feature or its Elixir step definitions, the existing iteration-061/066 discovery feature, the existing custom-group admission journey, or unrelated journeys.

Do not change application code, LiveView markup, routes, membership or messaging behavior, email templates, selectors, feature semantics, ADRs, project docs, the approved plan, or checked todo lines for this packet.

Do not bypass the browser interaction by dispatching `RequestGroupAccess` or targeted admission directly. Server-side setup and authoritative read-only assertions are appropriate, but request submission, email-link navigation, explicit Add, and welcome-link return must cross their real browser boundaries.
Do not treat accepted-for-send feedback as provider delivery, request submission or link opening as admission, Board admission as Admin conversation access, or the email URL as authority.

Do not broaden the browser suite, add arbitrary sleeps, create a second readiness/review loop, or run `dev check`, `dev check --quick`, `dev ci`, or another unscoped full-suite command; task 009 and the deterministic quality-gate node own iteration-wide validation.

references.facts: The one selected browser journey must cover the private placeholder, ordinary Admin email management link, mutation-free preview, explicit existing addition, welcome return, and unchanged requester privacy; the request is correspondence rather than authority or tracked state.

This is the approved 18-step journey. A targeted Cucumber dry run at the binding checkpoint found 16 undefined steps and two existing matches; remove only `@todo` after implementing those missing browser definitions.

symbols: person should see neither group conversations nor its membership list
references.facts: The existing privacy step already matches the journey and the file demonstrates stable group navigation and projection-aware assertions. Do not register a competing definition.
These accepted setup helpers create the named club, role assignments, ordinary membership, and custom Board state while maintaining the shared world maps used by member harnesses.

Existing support provides authoritative membership assertions and established welcome-email matching. The ordinary picker helper is not a substitute for the targeted email-link Add path in this journey.
Use separate reusable signed-in contexts for Eve and Dan, and keep scenario/mailbox state on the parent world so email-linked transitions remain coherent across actors.

Reuse projection-aware browser and mailbox primitives and the existing Admin-message absence assertion. Match fresh scenario emails by recipient, subject, and body/action rather than relying on mailbox order.
Accepted stable selectors expose the request action/status, targeted admission success, member rows, conversation/member sections, and absence of a composer for an outside member.
The accepted targeted panel exposes `#targeted-group-member-add`, identifies Eve and Board, and changes membership only on explicit click.
The dry-run contract requires every selected `@journey and not @todo` step to have exactly one definition, so enabling this feature must leave no undefined or ambiguous steps.
Browser-only journeys use `@journey`; `@todo` is removed only when the intended browser layer is executable and passing, while iteration tags retain provenance.
This deliberate cross-feature journey protects real browser boundaries without duplicating domain-rule permutations.

constraints: Use stable IDs, roles, URLs, and server-observable state; do not assert Tailwind classes, mailbox ordering, generated timing, or provider delivery claims.
Take mailbox baselines before the request and before explicit Add so the Admin request and welcome messages cannot be confused with sign-in or setup email.
Email lookup must tolerate asynchronous delivery through established bounded polling/dispatch helpers and select the correct fresh message by recipient and content.

The request action must run in Eve's context, the management link and Add in Dan's context, and the welcome return in Eve's context. Preserve host-aware club URLs and wait for connected LiveView state around interactive assertions.
Assert Eve is outside Board after request submission and again after Dan opens the email link; assert membership only after Dan clicks the explicit targeted Add action.
After admission, prove Board access without implying Admin access: Eve may enter Board's conversation surface but must not see or read the `Access request: Board` Admin conversation.
Keep task 008 limited to browser acceptance plumbing and the approved journey. Exact-state domain acceptance, all browser journeys, and the project-wide quality gate remain task 009.
completion_evidence_required: List every changed path and identify where the 16 previously undefined steps are implemented, which two existing definitions are reused, and where `@todo` was removed without changing scenario text or provenance.
Record the request-email and welcome-email baseline strategy and show that each fresh email is selected by the intended recipient, subject/content, and emitted link rather than mailbox position.
Show browser evidence that Eve sees Request access without a composer or protected Board content, clicks the real action once, and receives the accepted-for-send status.
Show authoritative membership evidence after request submission and after Dan opens the emitted targeted URL, both proving Eve remains outside Board before explicit confirmation.
Show Dan's browser follows the `Add Eve to Board` email action, sees the targeted Eve/Board control, clicks `#targeted-group-member-add`, and observes the accepted success/member-row state.
Show Eve's browser follows the emitted normal welcome link, can access Board's conversation surface, and still cannot see or directly access the Admin request conversation.
Show the journey-definition dry run has no undefined or ambiguous selected steps and the focused iteration-066 browser journey passes with its scenario and all 18 steps reported.
Record each focused validation command, working directory, exit status, scenario/step or test counts, and any unresolved issue. Do not report `dev check` for this packet.
